newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil gives up Spitzbergen acreage.
newsitem.headline: Statoil gives up Spitzbergen acreage.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday it had relinquished two out of four exploration licences in the Arctic archipelago of Spitzbergen.
Covering the Grimfjellet area in the South Spitzbergen national park and Agardh on the east coast, the acreage was licensed from the Norwegian state in the late 1970s.
Each licence, which is comparable with a block on the Norwegian continental shelf, covers about 10 square kilometres.
"After careful evaluation of relevant structures we have decided that these areas do not contain prospective oil and gas reserves," Ivar Pehrson, staff engineer, was quoted as saying.
"Although geological field trips identified interesting opportunities, seismic surveys have failed to find sufficiently large structures to give a positive net present value."
Statoil said plans for its two other licences in the area were under continuous review.
